ucs.title: [LLM] APT29 / Midnight Blizzard — OAuth illicit-consent + Service Principal secret addition to high-risk Graph scopes
ucs.description: Hunts the Midnight Blizzard (SVR / Cozy Bear) post-compromise pivot used against Microsoft Corporate (Jan 2024) and HPE: after a password-spray from residential proxies, the actor consents an OAuth app or adds new credentials/owners to an existing Service Principal with mailbox/full-tenant Graph scopes (Mail.Read, full_access_as_app, Directory.ReadWrite.All) to maintain persistent mail-reading access. The combination of audit-log action + privileged scope + non-admin or anomalous IP is the actor's signature, not generic OAuth abuse.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object) as targetSp values(All_Changes.object_attrs) as modifiedProps values(All_Changes.src) as srcIp values(All_Changes.user_agent) as userAgent from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product IN ("Azure AD","Azure Active Directory","Microsoft Entra ID") (All_Changes.action="Consent to application" OR All_Changes.action="Add service principal credentials" OR All_Changes.action="Add app role assignment to service principal" OR All_Changes.action="Add delegated permission grant" OR All_Changes.action="Add owner to service principal" OR All_Changes.action="Update application – Certificates and secrets management") by All_Changes.user All_Changes.action All_Changes.object _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | search (action="Consent to application" OR modifiedProps="*Mail.Read*" OR modifiedProps="*Mail.ReadWrite*" OR modifiedProps="*full_access_as_app*" OR modifiedProps="*Directory.Read.All*" OR modifiedProps="*Directory.ReadWrite.All*" OR modifiedProps="*EWS.AccessAsUser.All*" OR modifiedProps="*Application.ReadWrite.All*" OR modifiedProps="*RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory*") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
ucs.kql:
// APT29 / Midnight Blizzard - OAuth consent or SP credential add granting privileged Graph scopes
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let HighRiskScopes = dynamic([
    "Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Mail.Read.All","Mail.ReadWrite.All",
    "full_access_as_app","Directory.Read.All","Directory.ReadWrite.All",
    "Files.Read.All","Sites.Read.All","User.Read.All",
    "EWS.AccessAsUser.All","Application.ReadWrite.All",
    "RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where Application in~ ("Office 365","Microsoft Entra ID","Azure Active Directory")
| where ActionType in~ (
    "Consent to application.",
    "Add service principal credentials.",
    "Update application \u2013 Certificates and secrets management ",
    "Add app role assignment to service principal.",
    "Add delegated permission grant.",
    "Add owner to service principal.")
| extend RawProps = tostring(RawEventData)
| where ActionType =~ "Consent to application."
    or RawProps has_any (HighRiskScopes)
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IsAdminOperation,
          IPAddress, IsAnonymousProxy, CountryCode, ISP, UserAgent,
          ObjectName, ObjectId, ActivityObjects, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// APT29 / Midnight Blizzard - OAuth consent or SP credential add granting privileged Graph scopes
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let HighRiskScopes = dynamic([
    "Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Mail.Read.All","Mail.ReadWrite.All",
    "full_access_as_app","Directory.Read.All","Directory.ReadWrite.All",
    "Files.Read.All","Sites.Read.All","User.Read.All",
    "EWS.AccessAsUser.All","Application.ReadWrite.All",
    "RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory"]);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where LoggedByService in~ ("Core Directory","Application Proxy")
| where OperationName in~ (
    "Consent to application",
    "Add service principal credentials",
    "Update application \u2013 Certificates and secrets management",
    "Add app role assignment to service principal",
    "Add delegated permission grant",
    "Add owner to service principal")
| extend Target     = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName),
         ModProps   = tostring(TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties),
         InitUpn    = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName),
         InitIp     = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress),
         InitAppId  = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.appId)
| where OperationName =~ "Consent to application"
    or ModProps has_any (HighRiskScopes)
| join kind=leftouter (
    SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | project InitUpn = UserPrincipalName, SignInIp = IPAddress,
              RiskLevel = RiskLevelDuringSignIn, SignInCountry = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
  ) on InitUpn
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Target, InitUpn, InitIp, SignInIp, SignInCountry, RiskLevel,
          InitAppId, ModProps, Result, ResultDescription, CorrelationId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT29 Midnight Blizzard OAuth Consent or SP Credential Addition to High-Risk Graph Scopes
id: 9a3c2f1e-7d4b-4e8a-b6c0-3f1e2d4a7b88
status: experimental
description: Detects APT29/Midnight Blizzard tradecraft of adding OAuth consent or new credentials to a Service Principal carrying mailbox/full-tenant Graph scopes. Observed against Microsoft Corporate (Jan 2024) and HPE.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/01/25/midnight-blizzard-guidance-for-responders-on-nation-state-attack/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  consent:
    OperationName: 'Consent to application'
  cred_or_perm:
    OperationName:
      - 'Add service principal credentials'
      - 'Update application \u2013 Certificates and secrets management'
      - 'Add app role assignment to service principal'
      - 'Add delegated permission grant'
      - 'Add owner to service principal'
  scope_filter:
    TargetResources|contains:
      - 'Mail.Read'
      - 'Mail.ReadWrite'
      - 'full_access_as_app'
      - 'Directory.Read.All'
      - 'Directory.ReadWrite.All'
      - 'EWS.AccessAsUser.All'
      - 'Application.ReadWrite.All'
      - 'RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory'
  condition: consent or (cred_or_perm and scope_filter)
fields:
  - InitiatedBy
  - TargetResources
  - Result
falsepositives:
  - Approved SaaS / B2B app onboarding by Global Admin from corporate IP
  - Automated CI service principal rotation
level: high
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1098.001
  - attack.t1528
  - attack.t1550.001
  - threat.apt29
  - threat.midnight-blizzard
ucs.datadog_query: source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Consent to application" OR "Add service principal credentials" OR "Add delegated permission grant" OR "Add app role assignment to service principal" OR "Add owner to service principal") (@evt.name:"Consent to application" OR @properties.targetResources.modifiedProperties.newValue:(*Mail.Read* OR *Mail.ReadWrite* OR *full_access_as_app* OR *Directory.Read.All* OR *Directory.ReadWrite.All* OR *EWS.AccessAsUser.All* OR *Application.ReadWrite.All* OR *RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory*))
ucs.rationale: Generic OAuth-consent detections fire on every legitimate SaaS onboarding. APT29's documented playbook is specifically: (1) password-spray a low-priv tenant identity from a residential proxy, (2) leverage that account to consent or to add a new secret/owner to an EXISTING multi-tenant Service Principal already trusted with privileged scopes (full_access_as_app / Mail.Read / Directory.ReadWrite.All

ucs.title: [LLM] APT29 BEATDROP/ROOTSAW chain — explorer-spawned rundll32/regsvr32 loading DLL from mounted ISO/IMG/ZIP after browser drop
ucs.description: Hunts the APT29 (Cozy Bear / The Dukes) diplomatic-phishing loader chain documented by Mandiant and Microsoft: HTML smuggling drops an ISO/IMG/ZIP into the user's Downloads, the user mounts/extracts it, double-clicks a LNK, and explorer.exe spawns rundll32.exe (or regsvr32.exe / mshta.exe) executing a side-loaded BEATDROP/ROOTSAW/EnvyScout DLL from a non-System32 path. Correlates a browser-written container archive with a child rundll32 launched from explorer within four hours.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as dropTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Endpoint.Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","outlook.exe") (Endpoint.Filesystem.file_name="*.iso" OR Endpoint.Filesystem.file_name="*.img" OR Endpoint.Filesystem.file_name="*.vhd" OR Endpoint.Filesystem.file_name="*.vhdx" OR Endpoint.Filesystem.file_name="*.zip" OR Endpoint.Filesystem.file_name="*.rar") (Endpoint.Filesystem.file_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Endpoint.Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Endpoint.Filesystem.file_path="*\\INetCache\\*") by host Endpoint.Filesystem.user Endpoint.Filesystem.file_name Endpoint.Filesystem.file_path _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Endpoint.Filesystem)` | rename file_name as container file_path as containerPath | join type=inner host [| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as execTime values(Processes.process) as childCmd values(Processes.process_path) as childPath from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe" (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" OR Processes.process_name="regsvr32.exe" OR Processes.process_name="mshta.exe") (Processes.process="*.dll*" OR Processes.process="*.ocx*" OR Processes.process="*.cpl*") NOT (Processes.process_path="*\\Windows\\System32\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\WinSxS\\*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | where execTime >= dropTime AND execTime <= dropTime + 14400 | eval delayMin = round((execTime - dropTime)/60,1) | table dropTime execTime delayMin host user container containerPath process_name childCmd childPath
ucs.kql:
// APT29 - browser-dropped container + explorer-spawned rundll32/regsvr32/mshta loading non-System32 DLL
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowHours = 4h;
let Smuggled = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","outlook.exe","thunderbird.exe")
    | where FileName endswith ".iso" or FileName endswith ".img"
         or FileName endswith ".vhd" or FileName endswith ".vhdx"
         or FileName endswith ".zip" or FileName endswith ".rar"
         or FileName endswith ".7z"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\")
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Browser = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              Container = FileName, ContainerPath = FolderPath, ContainerSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".dll",".ocx",".cpl",".sct",".hta")
// Loader DLL must not live in trusted Windows directories
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Windows\System32\", @"\Windows\SysWOW64\", @"\Windows\WinSxS\"))
| join kind=inner Smuggled on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (DropTime .. DropTime + WindowHours)
| extend DelayMin = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, DropTime)
| project DropTime, ExecTime = Timestamp, DelayMin, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Browser, Container, ContainerPath, ContainerSHA256,
          LoaderBin = FileName, LoaderCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by ExecTime desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// APT29 - browser-dropped container + explorer-spawned rundll32/regsvr32/mshta loading non-System32 DLL (ASIM)
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowHours = 4h;
let Smuggled = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventType =~ "FileCreated"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","outlook.exe","thunderbird.exe")
    | where TargetFileExtension in~ ("iso","img","vhd","vhdx","zip","rar","7z")
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\INetCache\")
    | project DropTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname,
              ActorUsername, Browser = ActingProcessName,
              Container = TargetFileName, ContainerPath = TargetFilePath,
              ContainerSHA256 = TargetFileSHA256;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has "explorer.exe"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (".dll",".ocx",".cpl",".sct",".hta")
| where not(TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Windows\System32\", @"\Windows\SysWOW64\", @"\Windows\WinSxS\"))
| join kind=inner Smuggled on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (DropTime .. DropTime + WindowHours)
| extend DelayMin = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, DropTime)
| project DropTime, ExecTime = TimeGenerated, DelayMin, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          Browser, Container, ContainerPath, ContainerSHA256,
          LoaderBin = TargetProcessName, LoaderCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by ExecTime desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT29 BEATDROP/ROOTSAW Loader - Explorer Spawns rundll32/regsvr32/mshta with Non-System32 DLL
id: 4e8f2c9a-1b3d-4f6a-9c5e-7d2a1b8c3f04
status: experimental
description: Detects APT29 (Cozy Bear / The Dukes) HTML-smuggling loader chain where explorer.exe (from a mounted ISO/IMG or extracted ZIP) spawns rundll32/regsvr32/mshta against a DLL/OCX/CPL/HTA outside trusted Windows directories.
references:
  - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/tracking-apt29-phishing-campaigns
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/05/02/ransomware-as-a-service-understanding-the-cybercrime-gig-economy-and-how-to-protect-yourself/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.dll'
      - '.ocx'
      - '.cpl'
      - '.sct'
      - '.hta'
  filter_trusted:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\Windows\System32\'
      - '\Windows\SysWOW64\'
      - '\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not filter_trusted
falsepositives:
  - User double-clicks a legitimate signed installer CPL/OCX from Downloads
  - Third-party software updaters bundled in user-profile installers
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense-evasion
  - attack.t1027.006
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1218.011
  - attack.t1218.010
  - threat.apt29
  - threat.cozy-bear
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\Explorer.EXE OR *\\EXPLORER.EXE) @Image:(*\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RunDll32.exe OR *\\RUNDLL32.EXE OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\RegSvr32.exe OR *\\REGSVR32.EXE OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE) @CommandLine:(*.dll* OR *.DLL* OR *.ocx* OR *.OCX* OR *.cpl* OR *.CPL* OR *.hta* OR *.HTA*) -@CommandLine:(*\\System32\\* OR *\\system32\\* OR *\\SysWOW64\\* OR *\\syswow64\\* OR *\\WinSxS\\* OR *\\winsxs\\*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/explorer\.exe/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(rundll32|regsvr32|mshta)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\.(dll|ocx|cpl|hta|sct)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT regex("\\\\Windows\\\\System32\\\\", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| NOT regex("\\\\Windows\\\\SysWOW64\\\\", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| NOT regex("\\\\Windows\\\\WinSxS\\\\", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ucs.rationale: Bare 'explorer→rundll32' produces dozens of FPs/day, and bare 'browser drops ISO' is benign (developer images, software downloads). APT29's tradecraft is the specific chain: HTML-smuggled ISO/IMG container lands in Downloads via Chrome/Edge/Outlook (EnvyScout, ROOTSAW), the user mounts it, the bundled LNK fires rundll32 against a DLL/CPL whose path is NOT under %WINDIR%\System32 (BEATDROP, BOOMMIC
